metadata.scope: OSINT profiles for 5 Canadian MPs with high lobbying contact counts and YES votes on both MAID bills (C-14 and C-7)
metadata.methodology: Public sources only — OpenParliament, CBC, Globe and Mail, Global News, lobbying registry (lobbycanada.gc.ca), Ethics Commissioner records, parliamentary records, Wikipedia
metadata.notes: Lobbying contact counts sourced from federal Commissioner of Lobbying registry (lobbycanada.gc.ca). All information from publicly available sources.

profiles.name: Patty Hajdu
profiles.current_role: Minister of Jobs and Families; Minister responsible for the Federal Economic Development Agency for Northern Ontario (since May 2025)
previous_roles: Minister of Employment, Workforce Development and Labour (2017–2019)

controversies.title: COVID-19 pandemic preparedness failures
controversies.summary: As Health Minister, oversaw multiple pandemic response failures including the sidelining of the Global Public Health Intelligence Network (GPHIN) early warning system in May 2019. Admitted she knew nothing about GPHIN when she took over. Government discarded 2 million N95 masks and 440,000 gloves from the National Emergency Strategic Stockpile before the pandemic hit. Admitted Canada's stockpile was not prepared.

controversies.title: WE Charity scandal involvement
controversies.summary: As Health Minister during the WE Charity scandal, acknowledged PM Trudeau should have recused himself from the $900M student grant program awarded to WE Charity, which had financial ties to the Trudeau and Morneau families. Dismissed cover-up allegations.

controversies.title: Air Canada strike — Section 107 forced arbitration
controversies.summary: As Minister of Jobs and Families, invoked Section 107 of the Canada Labour Code less than 12 hours into the Air Canada flight attendants strike (10,517 workers), forcing binding arbitration. CUPE condemned the move as crushing Charter rights. Union defied the return-to-work order, with CUPE president stating they would risk jail. Part of a pattern of Liberal government using Section 107 against port workers, rail workers, and Canada Post.

controversies.title: Failure to end First Nations boil water advisories
controversies.summary: As Minister of Indigenous Services, oversaw continued failure to eliminate long-term boil water advisories despite Trudeau's 2015 promise to end them by March 2021. As of 2024, 28+ communities still under advisories. Neskantaga First Nation under advisory since 1995. Chief Christopher Moonias publicly accused her of forgetting the community at a Special Chiefs Assembly. One-third of on-reserve residents consider water unsafe.

controversies.title: Change.org petition for removal
controversies.summary: A public petition on Change.org calls for Hajdu's removal from office for incompetence.

lobbying_highlights: 302 registered lobbying communications in federal Commissioner of Lobbying registry
As Health Minister during COVID-19, was a top lobbying target — lobbyists scrambled to be heard on pandemic policy
Lobbying contacts span labour, transportation, international trade, agriculture, health, and industry sectors
Registry shows communications directed to ESDC, AAFC, Health Canada, House of Commons

maid_position.summary: Voted in favour of both Bill C-14 (2016, original MAID legislation) and Bill C-7 (2021, expansion of MAID including for mental illness)

foreign_connections.details: No specific foreign government connections identified in public records. Ministerial roles have been domestic-focused (status of women, employment, health, Indigenous services, jobs). Constituent case involving a Thunder Bay man trapped in Gaza was handled through Global Affairs.

financial_notes: Travel and hospitality expenses disclosed via proactive publication requirements (Access to Information Act amendments)
Disclosures available through House of Commons proactive publication system and departmental disclosure pages
No Ethics Commissioner findings against her identified in public records
key_votes: YES on Bill C-14 (Medical Assistance in Dying, 2016)

profiles.name: Ruby Sahota
profiles.current_role: Secretary of State for Combatting Crime (since May 2025)
previous_roles: Minister of Democratic Institutions and Minister responsible for FedDev Ontario (2024–2025)
Chair, Standing Committee on Procedure and House Affairs
Member, Standing Committee on Foreign Affairs and International Development

controversies.title: India foreign interference — ministerial role during inquiry
controversies.summary: As Minister of Democratic Institutions, co-issued the government statement on the Foreign Interference Commission's final report (January 2025). The inquiry found India used 'clandestine activities' and 'proxy agents' with 'illicit financial support' to interfere in the 2021 federal election. Sahota has stated India is still engaged in foreign interference and transnational repression. Served simultaneously as member of the Canada-India Friendship Group, raising questions about dual roles.

controversies.title: Trudeau India trip accompaniment
controversies.summary: Accompanied PM Trudeau on the controversial February 2018 state visit to India, which was widely criticized for the Atwal invitation scandal and perceptions of diplomatic mismanagement. Sahota was one of several Sikh MPs on the trip.

lobbying_highlights: 302 registered lobbying communications in federal Commissioner of Lobbying registry
As Minister of Democratic Institutions, was a target for lobbying on electoral reform and democratic processes
As Chief Government Whip, had significant influence over Liberal caucus discipline and legislative scheduling

maid_position.summary: Voted in favour of both Bill C-14 (2016) and Bill C-7 (2021) expanding medical assistance in dying

foreign_connections.details: Parents arrived from Punjab, India in the late 1970s. Father was Chairman of the Ontario Sikhs and Gurdwara Council. Member of the Canada-India Friendship Group. Listed on Indiaspora (organization tracking Indian-origin politicians globally). Accompanied Trudeau on 2018 India state visit. As Minister of Democratic Institutions, co-managed the government response to the Foreign Interference Commission which found India engaged in electoral interference.

financial_notes: No Ethics Commissioner findings identified in public records
Standard proactive disclosure of travel and hospitality expenses as cabinet minister
key_votes: YES on Bill C-14 (Medical Assistance in Dying, 2016)

profiles.name: Gary Anandasangaree
previous_roles: Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Canadian Heritage (Multiculturalism)

controversies.title: LTTE/Tamil Tigers immigration support letters
controversies.summary: Before joining cabinet, wrote letters on House of Commons letterhead to the Canada Border Services Agency urging approval of the immigration application of Senthuran Selvakumaran, whom Canadian officials had determined was a member of the LTTE (Tamil Tigers terrorist organization). CBSA reported Selvakumaran acknowledged working for the Tigers from 1992–1998. Federal Court rejected Selvakumaran's appeal in July 2025, upholding national security concerns despite the MP's support letter. Additionally, his office repeatedly inquired about the immigration case of a second Tamil Tigers member.

controversies.title: Phone number in RCMP terror finance probe document
controversies.summary: Phone number found in document seized during 2006 RCMP raid (Project Osaluki) on the Toronto offices of the World Tamil Movement (WTM), the alleged Canadian front organization for the Tamil Tigers. Document was filed in court as a 'Contact list of area coordinators.' WTM was added to Canada's terrorist entities list in 2008. Anandasangaree's office said he had no knowledge of how the list was found and was never contacted by law enforcement.

controversies.title: Self-recusal from Tamil-related national security files
controversies.summary: Less than one month after becoming Public Safety Minister, recused himself from any matters related to the LTTE or World Tamil Movement and asked officials to implement a 'screen' on Tamil community national security issues to avoid the appearance of conflict of interest.

controversies.title: Gun buyback leaked phone call
controversies.summary: A 20-minute phone call with his tenant was recorded and leaked to a gun owners' advocacy group. In the recording, Anandasangaree said the decision to ban 2,500+ assault-style weapon models was made to win votes in Quebec. Suggested police lacked resources to enforce the buyback. Offered to personally pay the difference between government compensation and what his tenant paid for banned firearms. Described his own comments as 'misguided' and 'in jest.' PM Carney expressed continued confidence. Conservatives demanded resignation. The leak occurred days before the government announced its gun buyback pilot program.

controversies.title: Calls for resignation — National Citizens Coalition and Conservative Party
controversies.summary: The National Citizens Coalition and Conservative Party have demanded Anandasangaree's resignation. The Globe and Mail editorial board published an opinion piece titled 'Gary Anandasangaree must resign as Public Safety Minister.' The Conservative Party created a dedicated webpage at conservative.ca/cpc/fire-minister-gary-anandasangaree/ and conservative.ca/gary-in-his-own-words/.

lobbying_highlights: 278 registered lobbying communications in federal Commissioner of Lobbying registry
As Minister of Crown-Indigenous Relations and then Public Safety, is a high-value lobbying target
Subject areas include public safety, national security, immigration, and Indigenous relations

maid_position.summary: Voted in favour of both Bill C-14 (2016) and Bill C-7 (2021) expanding medical assistance in dying

foreign_connections.details: Born in Jaffna, Sri Lanka (1973). Son of V. Anandasangaree, a leading Sri Lankan Tamil politician. Long-time advocate against human rights abuses during Sri Lankan Civil War. Attended UN Human Rights Council sessions. Championed parliamentary recognition of May 18 as Tamil Genocide Remembrance Day. Drove Canadian sanctions against Sri Lankan officials implicated in war crimes. Phone number found in 2006 RCMP seizure at WTM offices. Wrote immigration support letters for alleged LTTE member. Recused himself from LTTE/WTM national security files as Public Safety Minister.

financial_notes: No Ethics Commissioner formal findings identified in public records
Self-recusal from Tamil-related files suggests awareness of potential conflict of interest
Standard proactive disclosure of travel and hospitality expenses as cabinet minister
key_votes: YES on Bill C-14 (Medical Assistance in Dying, 2016)

profiles.name: Ron McKinnon
profiles.current_role: Member of Parliament; Vice Chair, Standing Joint Committee on Scrutiny of Regulations (45th Parliament, 2025–present)
previous_roles: Chair, Standing Committee on Public Safety and National Security (44th Parliament)
Chair, Standing Committee on Health (43rd Parliament)
Author of Bill C-224, Good Samaritan Drug Overdose Act (2017)

controversies.title: MAID expansion advocacy
controversies.summary: Voted to expand the euthanasia regime under Bill C-7, including extension to people suffering from mental illness alone. Spoke in the House in favour of Bill C-7. Also voted against pro-life Bill C-233 (to outlaw sex-selective abortion) in June 2021. Listed by Vote Pro-Life as consistently opposing pro-life positions.

controversies.title: Good Samaritan Drug Overdose Act — scope criticism
controversies.summary: Introduced Bill C-224 which received royal assent in May 2017 granting immunity from prosecution for simple possession when calling for overdose help. Critics argued the bill did not go far enough — no protection for those with outstanding warrants, breach of probation, or involved in more serious drug crimes. Studies showed fear of prosecution was only one of multiple barriers to calling 911 during overdoses.

lobbying_highlights: 274 registered lobbying communications in federal Commissioner of Lobbying registry
As Chair of the Standing Committee on Health (43rd Parliament), was a key target for health sector lobbying
As Chair of the Standing Committee on Public Safety and National Security (44th Parliament), was targeted by security sector lobbyists
Specific lobbying subjects include health, public safety, controlled substances policy

maid_position.summary: Voted in favour of both Bill C-14 (2016) and Bill C-7 (2021). Spoke in the House in support of C-7. Previously noted as a member of the Special Joint Committee on Medical Assistance in Dying.

foreign_connections.details: No specific foreign government connections identified in public records. Born in Alberta, background in computer technology (University of Alberta BSc, SAIT diploma). Parliamentary roles focused on domestic health and public safety policy.

financial_notes: No Ethics Commissioner findings identified in public records
Re-elected in 2025 with 47.4% of vote — his highest result

profiles.name: Darren Fisher
profiles.current_role: Member of Parliament for Dartmouth—Cole Harbour
previous_roles: Minister of Veterans Affairs and Associate Minister of National Defence (December 2024–March 2025)
Parliamentary Secretary to the Associate Minister of Health and Minister of Mental Health and Addictions (2023–2024)
Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Seniors (2021–2023)
Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Health (2019–2021)
Member, Special Joint Committee on Medical Assistance in Dying

controversies.title: Dartmouth Cove infilling — legal threats from developer
controversies.summary: Received a cease-and-desist letter from Atlantic Road Construction and Paving (ARCP) for encouraging residents to contact all levels of government to stop a proposed 2.7-hectare infilling of Dartmouth Cove. ARCP claimed they tried to contact Fisher 15 times through various channels without response. Fisher raised it in the House of Commons, stating he was elected to be the voice of his constituents. ARCP subsequently sued both Fisher and the Department of Fisheries and Oceans. DFO ultimately denied ARCP's infill application.

controversies.title: Brief tenure as Veterans Affairs Minister
controversies.summary: Served only 3 months as Minister of Veterans Affairs after being appointed in PM Trudeau's final cabinet shuffle following Chrystia Freeland's resignation. During this brief tenure, signed an MOU with Ukraine's Ministry of Veterans Affairs. The short appointment period limited his ministerial impact.

lobbying_highlights: 272 registered lobbying communications in federal Commissioner of Lobbying registry
As Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Health (2019–2021) during COVID-19, was a lobbying target for health sector interests
Health, mental health, seniors, and veterans affairs are key lobbying subject areas
His website features pharmacare as a priority policy issue

maid_position.summary: Voted in favour of both Bill C-14 (2016) and Bill C-7 (2021). Served as a member of the Special Joint Committee on Medical Assistance in Dying. As Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Health during C-7's passage, was closely involved in the MAID expansion.

foreign_connections.details: As Veterans Affairs Minister (Dec 2024–Mar 2025), signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Ukraine's Minister of Veterans Affairs, building on the security cooperation agreement between Trudeau and Zelenskyy.
